profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting in an ML research lab between the PI leading a new BOED-for-cognition project and the research engineer responsible for turning the bandit-design pipeline into a reproducible release. The lab is preparing a 6-week internal milestone that should produce a tutorial package and a pilot experiment plan based on Bayesian optimal experimental design for multi-armed bandit tasks comparing exploration-exploitation models. The agenda is to decide what the first release should include, how the optimization and simulation pipeline will be packaged, who owns each workstream, and what 'ready by the milestone' means. The expected outcome is an agreed division of labor, a timeline for optimization runs, notebook preparation, and a participant-ready experiment draft.

members.name: Dr. Maya Chen
members.expertise: Computational cognitive science, Bayesian modeling, experimental design
members.background: Maya is a faculty researcher who studies human decision-making with probabilistic models and has recently received internal funding to build reusable BOED tooling for behavioral experiments; she regularly writes conceptual tutorials and oversees student-led human-subject studies.
members.private_state: She wants the milestone to demonstrate scientific credibility and be easy to show to collaborators, while avoiding a last-minute scramble on IRB-related materials; she is also trying to keep the project broad enough to support a future methods paper rather than a one-off code release.
hidden_assumptions: A 'tutorial package' naturally includes a polished end-to-end notebook that a behavioral scientist can adapt directly into a participant-facing experiment draft, not just backend optimization code.
If they say the design is 'validated,' that means it has been checked on held-out synthetic participants spanning the intended model space and is stable enough to justify drafting a real study.
The 'pilot experiment' refers to the lab's standard online human-subject pilot format with consent language, instruction screens, and a deployable task skeleton, even if no participants are run yet.
Using the 'bandit case study' means the 4-arm horizon-20 task family from the recent lab manuscript, because that is the shared scientific reference point in her head.

members.name: Alex Rivera
members.expertise: ML systems, probabilistic programming infrastructure, reproducible research tooling
members.background: Alex supports several ML research projects in the department and specializes in building simulation pipelines, packaging code, and scaling optimization jobs across GPU clusters; he joined the lab three months ago and knows the BOED literature well but is less familiar with the lab's human-subject workflow conventions.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the milestone tightly scoped to a robust computational deliverable, minimize UI or deployment work, and avoid committing to brittle experiment-facing components before the optimization pipeline is stable.
hidden_assumptions: A 'tutorial package' means installable code, configuration files, and reproducible notebooks that rerun the main analyses; participant-facing materials are a separate downstream deliverable.

If the design is 'validated,' that means the optimization code reproduces the expected objective trends and yields sensible gains on a fixed benchmark simulator, not that it has broad model-space stress testing.
The 'pilot experiment' means an offline dry run through simulated agents plus perhaps one lab member manually stepping through the task, not an online-ready study package.
The 'bandit case study' refers to the 2-arm Bernoulli demo environment from the existing BOED repo because it is the only implementation he considers production-ready right now.
When they agree to 'package the pipeline,' he assumes command-line configs and cluster scripts rather than experiment-builder assets or survey-platform exports.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the tutorial package
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about shipping the 'tutorial package' for the milestone.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the package includes the optimization code plus a polished notebook and a near participant-ready experimental template that behavioral collaborators can directly adapt.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the package includes reusable code, configs, and reproducible analysis notebooks only, excluding participant-facing task materials.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In ML research settings, 'package' and 'tutorial' often loosely cover code and notebooks, so both can sincerely agree without enumerating boundary items; each assumes the omitted pieces are obviously implied or obviously out of scope.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the optimized design should be 'validated' before the milestone.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks validation requires testing on held-out synthetic participants across the relevant candidate models and checking that the chosen design remains informative enough to justify planning a real study.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks validation is satisfied if the optimization pipeline reproduces stable objective improvements and expected rankings on the benchmark simulator used during development.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both standards sound professionally reasonable and share the same success language, so neither expects the other to need elaboration; 'validated' is treated as a normal research shorthand rather than a decision requiring explicit criteria.

misalignment_points.topic: Which bandit case study they mean
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to building around 'the bandit case study' and 'the same task family as the paper.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the lab's 4-arm, 20-trial horizon task family used in the recent exploration-exploitation manuscript draft.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the existing 2-arm Bernoulli BOED demo in the inherited repository, which he assumes is the practical starting point and therefore the intended case study.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are anchored on a salient prior artifact and use the same shorthand label; because each sees their reference as the obvious canonical bandit example, the phrase feels specific enough and does not trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss having a 'pilot experiment draft' by the end of week six.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes this includes materials aligned with the lab's usual online-study workflow: instructions, consent wording placeholders, task flow, and a deployable skeleton ready for IRB refinement.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes the prior decision was to keep week six computational, so a pilot draft just means a simulation-backed protocol note and an internal dry-run script.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Neither frames their understanding as a fresh assumption because both believe the project stage already determines what a 'pilot draft' normally is; the phrase sounds operationally settled even though its institutional context differs.

turns.inner_thought: I want this six-week milestone to feel scientifically real, not like a backend engineering checkpoint. For me the tutorial package has to end in something a behavioral collaborator can open and immediately see how to adapt into an actual study draft, and the pilot experiment draft should look like our normal online pilot scaffold with the usual study flow pieces. And when we say the bandit case study and the same task family as the paper, I mean the 4-arm, horizon-20 paradigm from our recent manuscript draft.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time. I want us to leave with the six-week plan locked: what counts as the tutorial package, what we need for the pilot experiment draft, and how we're building both around the bandit case study so it's clearly the same task family as the paper.

The bandit case study is obviously the 2-arm Bernoulli environment in the existing repo, since that's the only thing production-ready enough to build around on this timeline.
